results.term_definition: A star with spectral type "K". Astronomers identify K-type stars by the presence of  very weak hydrogen lines but strong lines from iron and manganese atoms in their spectra. They have typical (effective) temperatures between around 3700 kelvins (K) and 5200 K. Compared to other stars, they appear orange-white to human eyes unless interstellar or atmospheric reddening is important. Examples of K-type stars are Aldebaran, in Taurus, and Pollux, in Gemini.
